positive: The official Requirements adapter exposes a read-only existing-run contract resolver that takes project root and run ID, calls the package-owned frozen binding resolver, and derives every required Requirements rule reference from that validated immutable pack.
Bundled-v2 ready resolution and bounded legacy-v1 read-only resolution remain distinct; legacy is attempted only when the bundled binding is categorically missing.
Every returned rule path remains inside the validated resolved pack, is a regular non-symlink file, and contains its required official marker.
Selector, process-cwd, and caller-manifest changes cannot affect the new resolver, while the existing pre-run stage_contract and public stage_request behavior remain unchanged for Phase 3.

The exact filtered proof collects three adapter tests covering four scenarios: frozen lookup and public-route preservation, bounded legacy fallback, and unsafe or incomplete state rejection. Its measured baseline has exactly three expected missing-API errors and no unrelated activation failures.
negative: Phase 2B.2 does not wire the resolver into stage_request, task-start, Planning Lock, MCP, or host projection before Phase 3 creates the binding.

The resolver never reads current.json, depends on process cwd, accepts caller manifest authority, contacts the network, executes pack content, writes state, provisions a pack, or creates or rewrites a binding.
Only a categorically missing bundled binding may attempt bounded legacy continuation; altered or incompatible bundled state never downgrades or falls back.
The filtered proof excludes unrelated activation tests and may not be broadened without a new approved proof boundary.
No package resolver, bridge, task-start, Planning Lock, MCP, host, schema, registry, CLI, or documentation owner is editable in this slice.
